findings.title: New snapshot hashes rejectable files before prior inventory/NPY byte-budget checks
findings.reproduction: Two bounded probes inserted either a tiny unknown foreign.bin or extended the existing head_weight.npy to a128MiB sparse logical file. A spy on the reviewed digest function aborts only if this invalid file reaches whole-file digest. Both hit the spy from _derived_snapshot line33 before cache.verify_role/_inventory/_npy could raise the expected bounded rejection. No128MiB data was read or allocated.
findings.actual_effect: digest is Path.read_bytes, so a genuinely oversized orphan/head/chunk/metadata file can allocate its entire byte size before the unchanged safety checks run. This weakens the prior bounded-header/inventory failure path; evidence proves call ordering, not an actualOOM benchmark.
findings.expected: Reject unknown namespaces, impossible NPY header/shape/file sizes, oversized metadata and inconsistent manifest byte bounds before payload hashing or reading. Snapshot work must not consume arbitrary untrusted file sizes before admission bounds.
findings.fix: Preflight exact allowed inventory and header/file-byte/metadata limits before capture, preserve evidence on refusal, and use streaming bounded-memorySHA. Reuse accepted _precheck/_inventory/_npy contracts as appropriate; explicitly bind cached-manifest size to the already-bound source-manifest size. Ensure the same ordering applies in initial and final snapshots, source9 and capacity collectors.
